Verify a File's SHA256 Against an Expected Digest

Source: R/lib_data_loader.R
vrfsha256.Rd

Computes the SHA-256 digest of a file and compares it with the digest pinned in a provenance record, so a pipeline can tell whether the file it downloaded is byte for byte the one the analysis was run on. A changed file (a silent re-release, a truncated download, an edited copy) gives a different digest.

Usage

vrfsha256(path, expsha)

Arguments

path

Path to the file to hash, a single string.

expsha

The expected SHA-256 digest: a hex string (64 characters, any case), or a length-1 list holding one, as read from provenance JSON.

Value

A list of three elements: actual (character, the computed digest, 64 lower-case hex characters), expected (character, the normalised expected value) and match (logical, TRUE when they are identical).

Details

The digest is computed by sha256file(), the package's own compiled SHA-256 core (FIPS 180-4), reading the file in chunks. The expected value is normalised before the comparison: a length-1 list (as loadprov() returns a pinned digest) is unlisted, surrounding spaces are trimmed and letters are lower-cased, so an upper-case digest copied from a web page still matches. The function reports and does not stop on a mismatch; the caller decides.

Errors: path that does not name a readable file; expsha that is not exactly one non-NA value.

Examples

f <- tempfile()
writeLines("hello capsule", f)

# Matching digest -> match TRUE.
chk <- vrfsha256(f, sha256file(f))
chk$match # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE

# A wrong expected digest -> match FALSE, with both values reported.
bad <- vrfsha256(f, strrep("0", 64L))
bad$match # FALSE
#> [1] FALSE
bad$actual # the real digest
#> [1] "55d6110230c260319d580bb6274db530b7e751c4f687fc00d0736ec531260a02"

# case and a list wrapper (as from provenance JSON) do not matter
vrfsha256(f, list(toupper(sha256file(f))))$match
#> [1] TRUE

# a missing file, or more than one expected digest, is an error
try(vrfsha256(file.path(tempdir(), "missing.csv"), strrep("0", 64L)))
#> Error : sha256file: /tmp/RtmpKWGbI3/missing.csv is not a file
try(vrfsha256(f, c("a", "b")))
#> Error : `expsha` must be a single SHA-256 hex string
